# Hash-pinned zizmor for the workflow-lint job in ci.yml. Copied from basetool-android (same version,
# same hashes) — keep the two in step when bumping.
#
# Why a requirements file at all: OpenSSF Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies check reports a bare
# `pip install zizmor==<version>` as unpinned, because a version is not a content hash. `pip
# install --require-hashes` is the fix, and it needs the digests in a file.
#
# Why pip rather than the checksum-verified tarball download ci.yml uses for actionlint: zizmor's
# GitHub release publishes no checksums file, so the tarball route would mean trusting a digest
# taken from a first download that nobody upstream asserts. PyPI publishes sha256 as first-class
# metadata and pip enforces it. That asymmetry is the reason the two tools are pinned differently.
#
# zizmor declares no Python dependencies (PyPI `requires_dist: null`) — it is a Rust binary shipped
# as a py3-none wheel — so this file is complete as written. Both Linux wheels are listed;
# ubuntu-latest selects the x86_64 one.
#
# NO DEPENDABOT ECOSYSTEM MAINTAINS THIS FILE. Version and hashes are bumped by hand, together, the
# same way ci.yml's ACTIONLINT_SHA256 is. Adding a `pip` entry to .github/dependabot.yml would not
# help: Dependabot rewrites hashes only for pip-compile output, which it detects by that tool's
# autogenerated header, so a bump PR against this file would carry stale hashes and land red.
zizmor==1.30.1 \
    --hash=sha256:eee12266b793cb87ad4a7e3af2e72404f8a63e3de5eb099b80bf7b1cfd232a8e \
    --hash=sha256:92906f448365672ebb657fb50d36f997290a3aaba8cac723214741ea9054845d
